_link.title: I can explain the spinal reflex as an unconscious response, describing the four steps and the role of the reflex arc

toLevel2.stem: What is the first step of the spinal reflex?
toLevel2.answer: Sensory receptors detect a stimulus and sensory neurons transmit the message to the spinal cord
distractors: The brain processes the stimulus and sends a command to the muscles to respond to the danger
Motor neurons transmit the message to skeletal muscles which carry out the automatic response
An interneuron in the spinal cord relays the message from the sensory neuron to a motor neuron

toLevel2.stem: What role does the interneuron play in the spinal reflex?
toLevel2.answer: It relays the message from the sensory neuron to a motor neuron
distractors: It detects the harmful stimulus at the site of contact
It sends the message to the brain for conscious processing
It carries the motor response to the skeletal muscles

toLevel2.stem: Why is the spinal reflex classified as an unconscious response?
toLevel2.answer: The motor response occurs before the brain registers the sensation
distractors: The brain initiates the response before the spinal cord is involved
The person is not awake when the spinal reflex takes place at all
The response involves only the autonomic nervous system division

toLevel2.answer: The path the neural signal travels during a spinal reflex
distractors: The shape of the spinal cord in the vertebral column
The curve of the motor neuron as it exits the brain
The distance between the receptor and the brain only

toLevel2.stem: In which step of the spinal reflex does the brain become aware of the sensation?
distractors: Step 1
Step 2
Step 3

toLevel2.stem: In a spinal reflex, the motor response occurs before the brain registers the sensation.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: The spinal reflex requires the brain to process the stimulus before the motor response can occur.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: In Step 2, an {{blank:1}} in the spinal cord relays the message from the sensory neuron to a motor neuron.

distractors: sensory neuron
motor neuron

toLevel2.stem: The spinal reflex is faster than a conscious response because the signal travels to the {{blank:1}} rather than the brain.

distractors: cerebral cortex
brain stem

toLevel2.stem: The path the neural signal travels during a spinal reflex is called the {{blank:1}}.

distractors: motor pathway
neural circuit

toLevel3.stem: Why is the spinal reflex faster than a conscious response?
toLevel3.answer: The signal only travels to the spinal cord, not to the brain
distractors: The brain processes the signal faster during a reflex response
Motor neurons travel faster during a reflex than during normal movement
Sensory receptors are more sensitive during a reflex than other responses

toLevel3.stem: What is the adaptive advantage of the spinal reflex?
toLevel3.answer: It allows the body to respond to danger before conscious awareness
distractors: It allows the brain to make a deliberate decision about the response
It prevents the body from ever experiencing pain from a stimulus
It ensures the person remembers the dangerous stimulus permanently

toLevel3.stem: Why does the brain register the sensation after the motor response has already occurred?
toLevel3.answer: The motor response is initiated at the spinal cord before the signal reaches the brain
distractors: The brain deliberately delays its processing to allow the reflex to complete first
Motor neurons transmit signals faster than sensory neurons in all circumstances
The brain is not involved in the spinal reflex at any point during the process

toLevel3.stem: What is the significance of the reflex arc in explaining the spinal reflex?
toLevel3.answer: It shows the shortest neural path for a rapid response
distractors: It describes how the brain processes all incoming signals
It explains why conscious responses are faster than reflexes
It illustrates how the ANS controls the reflex independently

toLevel3.stem: Why does Step 2 of the spinal reflex state that the response is initiated 'independently of the brain'?
toLevel3.answer: The interneuron relays directly to a motor neuron without brain involvement
distractors: The brain sends a command that arrives at the same time as the spinal signal
The brain is completely disconnected from the spinal cord during a reflex
The motor neuron receives the signal from the brain before the spinal cord

toLevel3.stem: Which division of the nervous system do the sensory and motor neurons of the spinal reflex belong to?
distractors: The autonomic nervous system
The central nervous system only
The sympathetic nervous system

toLevel3.stem: The spinal reflex provides an adaptive advantage because it allows a response to danger before the person is consciously aware of the threat.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: The spinal reflex is faster than a conscious response because the signal only needs to reach the {{blank:1}}, not the brain.

distractors: cerebral cortex
frontal lobe

toLevel3.stem: The adaptive advantage of the spinal reflex is that it allows the body to respond to {{blank:1}} before conscious awareness of the threat.

distractors: pleasure
learning

toLevel3.stem: The sensory and motor neurons in the spinal reflex belong to the {{blank:1}} nervous system, which is part of the PNS.

distractors: autonomic
sympathetic

toLevel4.stem: Ava touches an extremely hot pan and her hand jerks away before she feels the pain. Which step explains why she felt pain after the withdrawal?
toLevel4.answer: Step 4: the sensory message continued to the brain after the response
distractors: Step 1: the sensory receptors detected the pain before any motor response
Step 2: the interneuron sent the pain signal to the brain before the cord
Step 3: the motor neurons signalled pain to the brain during withdrawal

toLevel4.stem: A doctor tests Jake's knee-jerk reflex by tapping below his kneecap. Jake's leg kicks forward before he realises what happened. Which component of the reflex arc initiated the motor response?
toLevel4.answer: The interneuron in the spinal cord
distractors: The cerebral cortex in the brain
The frontal lobe of the brain only
The sensory receptor in the kneecap

toLevel4.stem: Mia steps on a sharp object and her foot lifts automatically. A student writes: 'The brain told her foot to move.' How should this be corrected?
toLevel4.answer: The spinal cord initiated the response; the brain was not involved until Step 4
distractors: The statement is correct because the brain always initiates motor responses
The brain initiated the response but the spinal cord carried it out for speed
The autonomic nervous system initiated the response, not the brain or cord

toLevel4.stem: A VCE exam question asks students to trace the neural pathway of a spinal reflex from stimulus to response. Which sequence is correct?
toLevel4.answer: Receptor, sensory neuron, interneuron, motor neuron, skeletal muscle
distractors: Receptor, motor neuron, interneuron, sensory neuron, skeletal muscle
Receptor, interneuron, sensory neuron, motor neuron, skeletal muscle
Receptor, sensory neuron, brain, motor neuron, skeletal muscle directly

toLevel4.stem: Tom writes that the spinal reflex involves the autonomic nervous system. Why is this incorrect?
toLevel4.answer: The spinal reflex uses sensory and motor neurons of the somatic nervous system
distractors: The spinal reflex only involves the central nervous system, not the PNS
Tom's answer is correct because reflexes are controlled by the ANS
The spinal reflex uses the sympathetic nervous system, not the somatic

toLevel4.stem: Ella wonders why she still feels pain after withdrawing her hand from a hot surface. Which explanation correctly applies Step 4?
toLevel4.answer: The sensory message continues to the brain, which registers pain after the response
distractors: Pain is felt before the hand is withdrawn because the brain processes first
Pain is generated by the spinal cord and does not require the brain at all
The motor response causes the pain sensation in the hand after withdrawal

toLevel4.stem: A student correctly identifies that a spinal reflex is unconscious. Which justification would earn full marks?
toLevel4.answer: The motor response occurs before the brain becomes consciously aware
distractors: The reflex does not involve any part of the nervous system at all
The person is unconscious and not awake during a spinal reflex
The brain initiates the response but the person does not remember it

toLevel4.stem: When Ava touches a hot pan, her hand withdraws (Steps 1-3) {{blank:1}} she consciously registers the pain (Step 4).

distractors: after
while

toLevel4.stem: The correct neural pathway sequence in a spinal reflex is: receptor, {{blank:1}}, interneuron, motor neuron, skeletal muscle.

distractors: motor neuron
interneuron

toLevel4.stem: A student who writes that 'the brain told the foot to move' during a spinal reflex should correct this to say the {{blank:1}} initiated the response independently of the brain.

distractors: cerebral cortex
frontal lobe

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that the spinal reflex does not involve the brain at all. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Partially correct; the brain registers the sensation in Step 4 after the response
distractors: Fully correct; the brain plays absolutely no role at any step of the reflex
Fully incorrect; the brain initiates the motor response in the spinal reflex
Partially correct; the brain initiates the reflex but does not process pain

toLevel5.stem: Dr Lee argues that the spinal reflex is a conscious response because the person eventually feels pain. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; conscious awareness occurs after the response, not before it
distractors: Correct; feeling pain proves the response was initiated with awareness
Correct; any response that produces a sensation must be classified as conscious
Incorrect; the spinal reflex does not produce any sensation of pain at all

toLevel5.stem: A student argues that spinal reflexes are slower than conscious responses because they involve more steps. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; reflexes are faster because the signal bypasses the brain
distractors: Correct; more steps always mean a slower overall response time
Correct; conscious responses are faster because the brain is quicker
Incorrect; both responses take exactly the same amount of time

toLevel5.stem: Emma claims that the reflex arc includes the brain because the signal eventually reaches it. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: The reflex arc describes the path for the motor response, which bypasses the brain
distractors: Correct; the brain is part of the reflex arc because it processes the stimulus
Correct; any neural path that eventually involves the brain includes the brain
Incorrect; the signal never reaches the brain during or after a spinal reflex

toLevel5.stem: A student writes that the spinal reflex uses the autonomic nervous system. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; the somatic nervous system provides the sensory and motor pathways
distractors: Correct; the autonomic system controls all involuntary and unconscious responses
Correct; the sympathetic division initiates all reflex responses in the body
Incorrect; the spinal reflex does not use any division of the nervous system

toLevel5.stem: Marcus argues that the spinal reflex is not truly 'unconscious' because the person becomes aware of the pain. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: The response itself is unconscious; awareness of pain occurs after the response
distractors: Correct; subsequent awareness of pain makes the entire reflex a conscious response
Correct; unconscious responses never produce any sensation or awareness at all
Incorrect; the person is never aware of pain after any spinal reflex has occurred

toLevel5.stem: A student suggests that the spinal reflex would be more effective if the brain were involved from the start. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; bypassing the brain is what makes the reflex fast enough to protect from harm
distractors: Correct; involving the brain would make the response more accurate and effective
Correct; the brain can process information faster than the spinal cord can manage
Incorrect; the brain is already involved from the start of every spinal reflex

toLevel5.stem: A researcher claims that all four steps of the spinal reflex occur simultaneously. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; the steps occur in sequence, with the motor response before brain awareness
distractors: Correct; all steps happen at the same instant during a spinal reflex event
Correct; neural signals travel so fast that sequencing is practically irrelevant
Incorrect; only the first two steps occur and the remaining steps are theoretical

toLevel5.stem: The claim that the spinal reflex does not involve the brain at all is {{blank:1}} because the brain registers the sensation in {{blank:2}} after the motor response.

distractors: fully correct
entirely wrong
Step 1
Step 2

toLevel5.stem: The argument that involving the brain would improve the reflex is {{blank:1}} because bypassing the brain is what makes the reflex {{blank:2}} enough to prevent injury.

distractors: correct
plausible
slow
